transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. What brings you in to see me?

Oh, hello Doctor. Thank you so much for having me... I really appreciate it, and I hope I'm not taking up time from people who are truly ill. 

Well, I suppose what brings me in is... well, for the past year or so, I just seem to be constantly on the go. I mean, I'm 87, so you'd think I'd be slowing down, right? But I actually have a terribly hard time just sitting down and being still. 

I try to make it useful, of course! I'm always puttering around the house, fixing little things, arranging the cabinets, or volunteering for just one more project. I really do just like to be helpful. But... I don't know, my family thinks it's a bit much, and it does feel like I just can't stop sometimes. Is that alright to say? I hope I'm explaining this the way you need me to.
Along with feeling restless, have you noticed your mood being unusually cheerful, elated, or full of energy lately?

Oh, goodness, no. I wouldn't say I'm unusually cheerful or elated... I mean, I'm just my normal self, really. I try to stay positive, of course, because nobody likes a grump, but I don't feel... abnormal about it, if that makes sense? 

I'm definitely not bouncing off the walls with some sort of strange energy. I just like to keep busy. I hope that's the right answer... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right idea. I don't feel like my mood is out of the ordinary at all.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot, more than you feel you should, about various things like health, family, or daily matters?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, of course, everyone worries a little bit about their family or, you know, making sure things are taken care of around the house... but I certainly don't sit around fretting all day. 

I really try to just take things as they come, and keep myself useful instead of stewing over what-ifs. It's no use making a fuss over every little thing, is it? I hope that doesn't make me sound careless! I just... I don't feel overwhelmed by worry or anything like that. Did I answer that right for you?
Have you noticed any physical changes recently, like unexplained weight loss, feeling unusually warm or sweaty, a racing heartbeat, or trembling hands?

Oh, no, nothing like that. My goodness, I hope I don't sound like I'm falling apart! My weight has been perfectly steady, and my heart feels just fine. No trembling or sweating, either. 

I really do try to take good care of myself, you know, eating right and all that. I certainly wouldn't want to be a bother to anyone by letting my health go. Everything physical seems to be in working order, thankfully. Is that what you were hoping to hear? I just want to make sure I'm not missing anything important you need to know.
Are you currently taking, or have you recently started, any new medications—such as anti-nausea drugs, antipsychotics, or other prescriptions?

Oh, heavens, no. I haven't started anything new. Certainly not any... what did you call them, antipsychotics? Oh my. No, nothing like that. Or anti-nausea pills, either. 

I try very hard not to take too many medicines if I can help it. I wouldn't want to be one of those patients who has a list a mile long and makes your job harder! I just stick to the absolute basics. So, no, nothing new at all. 

Is it alright that I'm not taking any of those? I just want to make sure I'm doing everything I'm supposed to, and I'd hate to think I missed something you wanted me to be taking.

Do you notice an uncomfortable or 'creepy-crawly' sensation specifically in your legs that makes you feel you have to move them, especially when you're sitting still in the evening or trying to fall asleep?

Oh, no, I wouldn't describe it like that. Creepy-crawly... oh, goodness, that sounds dreadful! No, my legs don't feel like that at all. 

Sometimes, I suppose, I just get a little restless, but I think that's just because I'm used to being up and about, keeping busy. It's perfectly normal to want to stretch your legs a bit before bed, isn't it? I certainly don't have any strange sensations keeping me awake. I try very hard to just settle down and get a good night's rest so I'm ready for the next day. 

I hope that's an alright answer? I just wouldn't want you to think I'm complaining about normal aches and pains, or making a fuss over nothing.
Do you often feel keyed up, on edge, or tense—like you can't relax—even when nothing specific is bothering you?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say I feel tense or on edge. I mean, we all have our moments where we have a lot on our minds, but I wouldn't say I feel keyed up for no reason. 

I really do try to keep a positive outlook and not let things get to me. It's so much better to just take a deep breath and find something useful to do, don't you think? I certainly wouldn't want to be one of those nervous types who worries over every little thing and makes everyone around them anxious, too. 

I just try to stay cheerful and keep moving forward. I hope that's the sort of attitude you like to see in your patients? I really do try my best to handle things well.
Does this constant need to keep moving or stay busy ever cause you real distress, or interfere with your ability to relax, sleep, or enjoy time with family?

Oh, distress? Well, I wouldn't say *distress*, exactly. That sounds so... so dramatic, doesn't it? I always try to be a pleasant person to be around. 

Though, I suppose... well, I did feel a little dreadful about a tiny incident recently. At the senior center, I’ve... well, I've actually had to apologize a few times after our committee meetings lately. I just get so eager to get things sorted out, I suppose I rush about a bit much. And... oh, it's a little embarrassing to admit, but one of my dear friends gently suggested that maybe I should take a smaller role at the morning sign-up table. She said my... my manner was making things a little tense for the others. 

I felt just terrible about it! I only ever want to be a help, never a hindrance. I just like keeping things moving so nobody has to wait in line. That's usually a good trait to have, isn't it? I certainly hope you don't think poorly of me for it... I really am trying to be more mindful of how I affect the other ladies. I just want to do the right thing.
When you do try to sit quietly or rest, do you notice any uncomfortable feelings of nervousness or unease building up inside you, or is it simply that you feel the urge to get up and do something?

Oh, it's certainly not a nervous feeling. Goodness, I wouldn't want you to think I'm sitting there stewing in anxiety or anything! It's really just... well, an urge to get up and be doing something, I suppose. 

Like, when I'm at the senior center meetings, or having to sit through those very long church announcements... I just get this silly little ants-in-my-chair feeling. It's nothing terrible, really! I just find myself needing to shift around a bit. Usually, I'll just quietly stand up to fetch a cup of coffee, or maybe straighten up the papers on the table just to get through the slower parts. 

It's just me trying to be helpful while I'm up, you know? I hope that makes sense? I just much prefer to be useful rather than sitting perfectly idle, if that's an alright way to be.
Has this restless, need-to-keep-busy feeling been a lifelong part of your personality, or did it start or noticeably worsen sometime in the past year or two?

Oh, well, I've always liked to be a doer, you know. I think being active is a good thing! But... I suppose it hasn't always been quite this noticeable. 

If I'm being perfectly honest—and I do want to give you the right answers—it's really been standing out more for, oh, maybe a year and five months or so? I... well, I had a bit of a stressful patch. Just some unexpected insurance bills, and a few home repairs that suddenly needed doing. Nothing I couldn't handle, of course! But it did push me into taking on a lot more at the senior center, just to keep my mind occupied and make sure I was still being useful. 

That's a perfectly normal way to handle a little extra on your plate, isn't it? I certainly hope you don't think I'm complaining... I just naturally try to keep busy when things pile up, if that makes sense?

Are those stressful issues, like the insurance bills and home repairs, resolved now, and if so, has the restless, need-to-keep-busy feeling continued just as strongly even without those specific stressors present?

Oh, the bills and repairs? Yes, yes, thankfully those are all sorted out now. My nephew was such a dear, he came over and helped me make sense of the paperwork, and the handyman fixed the roof right up. So that's all behind me now, which is a blessing. 

But... well, I suppose the busy feeling hasn't really gone away. I'm still buzzing about just as much as I was then. I just... I suppose I got so used to being on the go, it's become a bit of a habit? I still find myself volunteering for everything and rushing around the center, even though I don't really *need* the distraction anymore. 

I hope that doesn't sound foolish. It's just... once you get used to being the one who gets things done, it's hard to just stop and sit still, isn't it? I'm sure you see that all the time with people my age... wanting to stay active and helpful. It's better than just sitting in a rocking chair all day, right?
{"intent": "Assess whether the restlessness is accompanied by irritability or frustration

Oh, goodness, no! Irritable? Frustrated? Oh, I certainly hope I don't come across that way to anyone. I really try my best to be a pleasant person to be around, you know? 

It's really not an angry or upset sort of feeling at all. Like I said, it's just a little bit of... well, extra energy, I suppose. Just a strong desire to be up and doing something useful. I don't get cross with people or feel frustrated about it. I just want to be helpful! 

I would feel just awful if anyone thought I was being irritable with them. I'm just trying to keep busy and make sure everything is taken care of. That's a good way to look at it, don't you think? I certainly try to keep a smile on my face through it all.
Over this past year or so, have you noticed that you need less sleep than you used to—waking up early or feeling fully rested after just a few hours—without feeling tired the next day?

Oh, my sleep? No, no, I certainly still need my rest! If I don't get a proper night's sleep, I definitely feel it the next morning. 

I'm not one of those people who can just bounce out of bed after three or four hours and feel fine, goodness no. I always try to be sensible and get to bed at a reasonable hour. I think a body just needs its rest, especially at my age, right? 

I do try my very best to take good care of my health that way, making sure I get enough sleep so I can be useful the next day. It's so important to keep a good routine, don't you agree? I certainly hope I'm doing that part right, at least!
When you're working on a task or project, do you find it hard to let others help or do it their own way, because you feel it has to be done exactly right or it won't be good enough?

Oh, goodness, no. I would never want to be one of those bossy people who dictates how everything must be done. If someone is kind enough to offer their help with a project, I'm just so, so grateful to have it! 

I certainly don't stand over them and nitpick or demand it be done exactly my way. I mean, I like things to turn out nicely, of course, but I'm more than happy to let people do things their own way. It's the teamwork and the company that really matters, isn't it? 

I always try to be very appreciative of anyone's time. Nobody likes a micromanager, right? I really do hope people find me easy and pleasant to work with. I would just hate to think I was making anyone feel like their help wasn't good enough for me.

Oh, no, I wouldn't say I feel tense or on edge. I mean, we all have our moments where we have a lot on our minds, but I wouldn't say I feel keyed up for no reason. 

I really do try to keep a positive outlook and not let things get to me. It's so much better to just take a deep breath and find something useful to do, don't you think?
